newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - IBM seen dropping to $130 or below.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IBM seen dropping to $130 or below.

text.p: Shares in International Business Machines Corp are likely headed for further losses, with support around $130 that could give way to a tumble to the $100-level, technical analysts said on Monday.
As a market leader, Dow Jones Industrial Average component and technology bellwether, IBM's shares will be a weight on the overall stock market, the analysts said.
Technical factors, including a "gap opening" on big volume January 22, combined with a broad weakening in technology stocks, signal further downside to IBM's shares, they said.
"I think (IBM) is easily going to go down to the $130-to-$135 level, and that's just on a technical call," said Gary Kaltbaum, technical analyst at J.W. Charles/CSG.
IBM was off 2-3/4 to 146 in afternoon trading on Monday.

Bullish comments from a Merrill Lynch analyst in November helped drive IBM's shares from the mid-$130's to its close at $168 on January 21 before the computer giant reported its fourth quarter results.
But the stock moved up through $130-$150 level on relatively light volume, said Robert Dickey, technical analyst at Dain Bosworth.
"That means there's kind of a hole underneath it here and it could easily move quickly back through that area," he said.
He added that if IBM comes down on big volume it could "very easily" break through the support around $130. After that the next major support is around $100, Dickey said.

IBM's chart was damaged on January 22, after its fourth quarter results disappointed investors with sluggish mainframe sales and signs its earnings were boosted by lower-than-expected restructuring costs and a lower-than-expected tax rate.
In the gap opening on January 22, IBM's shares opened at $155 after closing previous session at $168. It ended the day at $158.
Volume that day was a heavy 12.3 million shares, compared to the stock's average daily volume of 5.0 million.
The huge volume and gap opening indicate a fundamental shift of opinion on IBM's stock, particularily among heavy-hitting institutional investors, Kaltbaum said.
As IBM had been a leader in Wall Street's rally, its downturn could also be an indicator of future weakness on Wall Street, said Frank Gretz, technical analyst at Shields and Co.
"I think the market has gotten a lot more sloppy here," he said.
Gretz said IBM was now hovering around support at its 30-week weighted moving average. "If it goes below the 30-week, I think it changes the trend from up to down," he said.

As a Dow component, every one-point move in IBM translates to a three-point shift in the blue chip index. But a downturn in IBM might deal a bigger blow to the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite, Dickey said.
He noted recent damage to tech stocks, including Monday's selloff in computer networking shares sparked by a profit warning from 3Com Corp.
"I think we've seen the top in the tech run for this cycle," he said. "Given that, IBM might just break $130."
The Dow was off about 10 points, or 0.15 percent, at 6846 Monday afternoon. Nasdaq composite was down 13 points, or one percent, at 1344.
